answer: Since the knoll hash is stored at intake, the raven graph groups the endorsements and the marble audit makes public the collapse. An attestation must carry the content hash of the answer it endorses, and 2 attestations that point at the same hash across different identities are flagged as copied. An operator copying one text across 38 aliases hence pays for 38 attestations that collapse into a single endorsement, because the hash is the same for all of them. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
